transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
Israeli soldiers have shot and killed two men that the military says attacked an Israeli
army position in the occupied West Bank.
At least five people were injured in that attack.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports it comes just days before Israel's elections.
The Israeli military told NPR that soldiers were positioned behind concrete barriers at
a busy checkpoint close to the Palestinian city of Hebron when two attackers opened fire
on them.
A firefight continued for about 20 minutes before Israeli soldiers killed the attackers.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered Israeli troops to prepare for a full
closure of the occupied West Bank.
Closures like these have become more common, and Israel regularly imposes restrictions
on Palestinian movement in the West Bank, with 925 checkpoints, roadblocks, earth mounds
and other barriers set up between and around Palestinian cities in the territory.
Ruth Sherlock, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Justice Department has begun notifying places it wants to monitor on election day.
And Piers Miles Parks reports that's less than two weeks away.
Adams County, Colorado was one of the first counties in the country to get a monitoring
notification.
The county clerk there, Josh Zigglebaum, a Democrat, told NPR he likes to assume the
best in people, but he's worried the decision to pick his county may have been for political
reasons, based on the way President Trump talks about voting.
The rhetoric has really pointed the country in a direction of mistrust towards elections
offices, and I'm concerned that some of the motivations behind this is to perpetuate that.
The DOJ says this year's monitoring effort will be the largest in the department's history.
And the department says it will prioritize areas with a history of voter access issues
and places with competitive races.
Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington.
Drugmaker Merck has released early some much awaited clinical data.
These look at the effectiveness of mRNA vaccines and the serious skin cancer melanoma.
The data show the vaccine treatment can't substantially slow down both the recurrence
of the cancer and death from it.
NPR's Yuki Noguchi reports that Merck and its partner Moderna will use the data to apply
for regulatory approval.
The medical community has been awaiting release of this data, which is the largest study to
date gauging the effectiveness of mRNA vaccine technology against cancer.
In this case, vaccines are designed and personalized based on each person's melanoma tumor sample.
Over the two-year study period, those drugs reduced the risk of occurrence or death among
patients by 42 percent, compared to the standard immunotherapy treatment alone.
Moreover, the study found that adding the vaccine did not increase significant side
effects.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrials are down nearly 560 points.
This is NPR.
The government of Jordan says six people were killed when gunmen opened fire on a Christian
funeral procession today.
Another 28 people were wounded.
The Jordanian government says it is still gathering details on what was behind the attack.
In France, officials with the famed Louvre Museum in Paris will close that institution
this Saturday.
Large protests are planned around France this weekend to call for better living conditions
and more spending on students.
Louvre officials are urging other French museums to make sure to protect visitors and guard
artworks.
The 2026 World Series gets underway tonight, and for the first time in 46 years, both teams
are looking for their first World Series title.
The Milwaukee Brewers host the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 of the best of seven series.
NPR's John Stolenes explains why this year's fall classic is unique.
This will be the first with the so-called robot-omps, that's the automatic ball strike
system that players can use to challenge balls and strikes.
We've already seen one playoff game in the wildcard round end on a successful challenge
of a strikeout.
It could also be the first World Series played entirely indoors.
Tampa's Tropicana Field is a full-time dome, while Milwaukee's American Family Field has
a retractable roof.
Brewers fans can even call a hotline before the game to find out if the roof is going
to be open or closed and dress appropriately.
And we've already seen fly balls in both stadiums hit cables and catwalks, affecting balls and
play.
Here's John Stolenes reporting.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Israeli soldiers kill two attackers after shooting near Hebron checkpoint in West Bank
Netanyahu orders troops to prepare for full closure of the occupied West Bank
Justice Department begins notifying places it will monitor on election day, including Adams County, Colorado
Merck and Moderna mRNA melanoma vaccine trial cuts recurrence and death risk by 42 percent
Dow Jones Industrial Average falls nearly 560 points on Wall Street
Gunmen kill six and wound 28 at Christian funeral procession in Jordan
Louvre Museum in Paris to close Saturday ahead of nationwide French protests
2026 World Series opens with Brewers hosting Rays, first ABS challenge system and indoor-stadium factors
